messages:
acme_integration: Hey team — since we flipped on function-calling + structured-output for our chat pipeline yesterday, p95/p99 for generate requests spiked. p95 from ~380ms -> ~650ms, p99 to ~1.1s. Request id: r-0a1b2c3d. Repro steps below, hitting timeouts in prod. Can someone take a look?

alex_support: Thanks, pinging SRE and runtime. Can you paste a minimal request (model, token counts, tools list, schema) so we can repro? Also which region/cluster.

acme_integration: Minimal repro (we're using hosted-us-east-1):

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model":"rwft-large-02",
    "input":"Summarize actions",
    "max_tokens":256,
    "tools":["search","calendar"],
    "structured_output": {
      "schema": {
        "type":"object",
        "properties":{
          "tasks":{ "type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"title":{"type":"string"},"due":{"type":"string","format":"date"}}}}
        }
      },
      "strict": true
    }
  }'

Note: average input tokens ~40, output tokens ~120.

maria_sre: I pulled traces for r-0a1b2c3d from APM. Span breakdown (sample):

```
TraceID: r-0a1b2c3d
spans:
 - parse: 12ms
 - tool-router: 95ms
 - schema-validate: 78ms (synchronous, in-runtime)
 - model-infer: 45ms
 - response-serialize: 9ms
 - network: 22ms
Total wall: ~261ms for this trace but p95/p99 skewed because validation+router serialized many requests causing queueing -> p95/p99 higher (observed p95 ~650ms).
```

kevin_runtime: Looks like the schema validator change in schema-validator v1.2.0 is the culprit. It switched to full JS regex + deep-ref validation and is executed inline inside the tool-router process. That means each structured-output request blocks the router until validation completes.

jessica_prod: Are we seeing errors or just latency? How widespread?

maria_sre: Error rate hasn't gone up, just latency SLO violations and longer tail. From the last 3 hours: ~8% of generate requests used structured-output. For the ACME tenant specifically, ~4.8k calls/hr -> their p95 increased and they're hitting app-level SLOs.

alex_support: Short-term mitigations? Customers are complaining.

kevin_runtime: Short-term options (fastest to implement):
1) Per-request flag to bypass server-side strict validation: "structure_validation":"off" (server will still return unvalidated JSON).
2) Rollback schema-validator to v1.1.4 which did lighter-weight checks.
3) Add schema-hash cache so repeated schema validations are O(1) lookup.
4) Route structured-output requests to a separate pool to avoid queueing main router.

maria_sre: Operationally I'd prefer (2) + (3) as hotfixes: rollback to v1.1.4 on prod canaries + enable validator cache globally. I'll run a canary ASAP and monitor p95/p99.

alex_support: Can you give me the exact curl to toggle the flag so I can tell ACME how to bypass quickly?

kevin_runtime: Use this for now:

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwft-large-02","input":"...","structured_output":{"schema":{...},"strict":false},"structure_validation":"off"}'

Note: this will skip server-side strict validation and should shave ~70-120ms off each call per trace.

schema-lint-bot: Suggestion: also enable schema hash bloom cache with TTL 1h to reduce CPU for repeated schemas. Sampling validation on 10% of requests preserves quality checks.

deploy_bot: Started rollout: schema-validator v1.1.4 -> canary pool (pool-id: sv-canary-3).

maria_sre: Canary metrics after 10m: p95 for canary decreased from ~620ms -> ~390ms, p99 down to ~720ms. Queue length on tool-router dropped by 60%. Pushing rollback to small fraction of production now.

kevin_runtime: I'll open PR for async validator worker + schema-hash cache (PR #4821). Will also add per-schema instrumentation so we can see heavy schemas. ETA: PR by EOD, bench tests tomorrow.

jessica_prod: Product notes: communicate mitigation and ETA to ACME. Also track other tenants who enabled structured-output; run a tenant-wide scan to detect sudden QoS changes. I'll prepare customer communication template.

alex_support: Draft message to ACME: "We identified that strict server-side schema validation is increasing tail latency for structured-output requests. Short-term: you can add \"structure_validation\":\"off\" to your request to bypass server validation; we are rolling back the heavier validator and will follow up with permanent optimizations and a timeline." Can someone approve?

maria_sre: Approved. Also advise them to keep tool list minimal while we stabilize.

acme_integration: Thanks — we'll add the bypass for now and reduce tool calls. Please keep us posted. Appreciate the fast follow.

kevin_runtime: Long-term fixes (tracked in ENG-1234):
 - async/off-thread schema validation (WASM or native) to avoid blocking router
 - schema-hash cache for O(1) validation hits
 - streaming/incremental validation during token generation (validate partial JSON as it's produced)
 - per-tenant routing to dedicated pools for heavy structured-output users
 - add sampling + alerts for validator CPU/opcost spikes

alex_support: I updated the ticket with canary metrics and customer mitigation steps. If canary stays green for 30m we push rollback and close incident.

deploy_bot: Rollback complete: schema-validator v1.1.4 rolled to 20% of prod (start 1729460000). Monitor dashboards for tail latency.

maria_sre: Early post-rollback numbers: tenant p95 trending back to ~420ms, p99 down to ~650ms. Still above baseline but much improved. Further improvements expected after cache + async work.

schema-lint-bot: Add follow-up tasks: add validator benchmarks to release gating, create perf smoke tests for structured-output paths.

alex_support: Closing loop with ACME now. Will reopen if they see issues after toggling. Thanks everyone.

acme_integration: Confirmed — after adding structure_validation off, their internal 95th dropped ~45%. Will monitor overnight and report any regressions.

kevin_runtime: I'll push the PR and a perf test matrix tomorrow morning. Thanks all.
